notes: Copilot's in-REPL reset ROTATES the session id: /clear and /new both call clearHistory, which creates a new session and switches to it (CLI 1.0.77 bundle, app.js @8632467). The recipe sends /clear, because only /clear (abandon:true) also closes and evicts the outgoing session — /new may keep it alive as a background session. Shape: the v1 birth is the two-phase presession model the copilot column uses (proc-<PID> row first, then the real <session-id> once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt); v2_session_birth carries new_session:true so it can match NEITHER the proc- row NOR the first real session; old_session_ended asserts transcript_removed for the FIRST real session and is anchored to v2_session_birth (not to the reset) because PIDManager's same-PID cleanup fires at the NEW session's pid_discovered, i.e. after B is already visible. v2_session_birth's 90 s window is deliberately wide: the post-reset directory mints nothing until the next prompt writes events.jsonl into it (sessionIDFromPath accepts only that constant filename). PROVISIONAL on one point — whether the daemon first observes the post-reset session in ready or straight into working is a race unsettleable from source, since events.jsonl already holds session.start … user.message when it first appears; if record finds it born working, drop v2_session_birth and move new_session:true onto v2_turn_start, leaving every other phase unchanged. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only auto and the router picks gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
The first real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, born ready
First user prompt drives the real session ready → working (user.message)
assistant.turn_end settles the first turn back to ready on the pre-reset session

Spec: 'New session appears in ready with a NEW session_id' — after /clear, a session id matching neither the proc-<PID> row nor the pre-reset session. The window is wide because the new session-state/<newid>/ directory is invisible to the daemon until the next prompt writes events.jsonl into it.

Spec: 'Old session disappears' — PIDManager's same-PID cleanup emits transcript_removed for the PRE-RESET session once the new session claims the same (cwd-bound) PID. Anchored to v2_session_birth because the cleanup fires at the new session's pid_discovered, which necessarily follows its birth.
Second user prompt drives the NEW session ready → working (must not match a stale transition on the pre-reset session)
Second turn completes back to ready on the new session; final state is ready
